Adventure Riding Without Breaking the Bank

You do not need a twenty-thousand-pound BMW GS to enjoy adventure touring. Several new bikes under seven thousand pounds offer genuine adventure capability, and the used market opens up even more options. These budget adventure bikes prove that the quality of the adventure depends on the rider, not the price tag.

New Bikes Under Seven Thousand

Royal Enfield Himalayan 450 — At around five thousand pounds, the new Himalayan is the budget adventure king. The 452cc single is torquey and economical, the chassis is surprisingly capable off-road, and the overall package is endearingly simple. It will not win any drag races but it will take you anywhere in Britain with a smile.

Honda CRF300 Rally — Honda's small adventure bike at under six thousand pounds. The 286cc single is peppy and incredibly fuel-efficient. Light at 153kg, it is genuinely enjoyable on green lanes and byways. Limited luggage capacity and motorway comfort but outstanding on B-roads.

Suzuki V-Strom 650 (new) — The evergreen V-Strom starts around seven thousand pounds new. The 645cc V-twin is smooth, reliable, and economical. It is not exciting but it is deeply competent and has an enormous owner community for advice and aftermarket support.

Used Bargains Under Seven Thousand

BMW F 850 GS (2018-2021) — The middleweight GS offers genuine BMW adventure capability at used prices. The 853cc twin is lively and the electronics are comprehensive. Five to seven thousand buys a well-maintained example.

Triumph Tiger 800 XCA (2015-2019) — The previous-generation Tiger with its characterful triple engine. Off-road capable with wire wheels and long-travel suspension. The XCA spec includes full electronics and heated grips. Four to six thousand pounds.

KTM 790 Adventure (2019-2021) — The original middleweight adventure from KTM with an outstanding engine. Sharp handling and excellent off-road ability. Five to seven thousand for good examples. Read our Adventure Bikes Compared: The Top 10 for UK Touring 2026 guide for more. Read our Mid-Weight Adventure Bikes for UK Touring guide for more.

Making a Budget Bike Tour-Ready

  • Luggage — Soft panniers from Oxford or Kriega cost under two hundred pounds and provide adequate touring capacity.
  • Screen — A taller aftermarket screen improves comfort dramatically for under one hundred pounds.
  • Protection — Crash bars and hand guards protect your investment in drops. Budget two hundred pounds.
  • Comfort — A gel seat pad or sheepskin cover improves comfort for under fifty pounds.
The best adventure is the one you actually go on. A budget bike with worn luggage and a scratched screen has more touring credentials than a showroom-fresh GS that only rides to the cafe on sunny Sundays. Get out there and ride.
keyTakeaways: Genuine adventure capability is available new for under seven thousand pounds.
The Royal Enfield Himalayan 450 is the budget king at around five thousand pounds.
The used market opens up the BMW F 850 GS and KTM 790 Adventure at these prices.
The Honda CRF300 Rally is light at 153kg and superb on green lanes.
A few hundred pounds of luggage, screen and protection makes any bike tour-ready.

comparisonTable.caption: Adventure bikes under seven thousand pounds

pros: Real adventure capability without a twenty-thousand-pound outlay.
Small singles are light, frugal and enjoyable on green lanes.
Used middleweight GS and KTM options deliver big-bike ability cheaply.
cons: Small-capacity bikes offer limited motorway comfort and luggage space.
Used bargains may need consumables and lack warranty cover.

faq.q: What is the best value new adventure bike?
faq.a: The Royal Enfield Himalayan 450 at around five thousand pounds is the budget adventure king. The 452cc single is torquey and economical, the chassis is surprisingly capable off-road, and the simple package will take you anywhere in Britain, even if it will not win any drag races.

faq.q: Can I get a proper middleweight on a budget?
faq.a: Yes, on the used market. The BMW F 850 GS from 2018-2021 offers genuine BMW adventure capability for five to seven thousand pounds, and the KTM 790 Adventure delivers an outstanding engine and sharp off-road ability for similar money. Both need careful inspection at this price.

faq.q: How do I make a budget bike tour-ready?
faq.a: Soft panniers from Oxford or Kriega cost under two hundred pounds, a taller screen improves comfort dramatically for under one hundred, and crash bars with hand guards run about two hundred. A gel seat pad or sheepskin cover adds comfort for under fifty pounds.

faq.q: Is a small single enough for touring?
faq.a: The Honda CRF300 Rally is peppy, frugal and light at 153kg, making it genuinely enjoyable on green lanes and B-roads. The trade-offs are limited luggage capacity and motorway comfort, so it suits riders prioritising back-road exploration over long, fast dual-carriageway stints.
